newsitem.title: UK: Salary row as income falls at UK Camelot.
newsitem.headline: Salary row as income falls at UK Camelot.

text.p: British national lottery operator Camelot Plc on Wednesday announced a decline in the money it raised for good causes as its critics seized on confirmation of over a 40 percent hike in directors' salaries.

Camleot said total sales in the year to end-March fell 10 percent to 4.7 billion pounds ($7.7 billion). It said profit after tax fell from 51.1 million pounds to 46.8 million while sums raised for good causes dropped to 1.27 billion from 1.42 billion.
Camelot was forced to bring forward the release of the figures by several days after they were leaked to a weekly trade magazine.
Criticism of Camelot's directors, dubbed "fat cats" by the British press, was renewed after it emerged that their total earnings had spiralled to 2.35 million pounds.
The new Labour government, which has vowed to bring in a non-profit lottery operator when Camelot's licence expires in 2001, said it would outline proposals for reforming the lottery in July.

"It is the people's money and I am determined it should work in their interests," Chris Smith, the minister responsible for arts and culture said in a statement, responding to press speculation on Camelot's results. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
